title: telemetry
description: Daemon -> client, every ~50 Hz tick. state/currents are lerobot dicts. The periodic block (loop_hz..status) appears every TELEMETRY_INTERVAL ticks.

currents.description: Signed raw Present_Current per motor (virtual-tactile / haptics).

robot_mic_live.description: INJECTED BY THE BRIDGE, not the daemon: the L2 media bridge adds this to every relayed telemetry frame. The daemon never sends it. Consumers must accept it here even though it is not a daemon field, because the frame a client receives is the bridge's, not the daemon's.

robot_local_mic_muted.description: Bridge-injected. Robot-side local mute; robots boot muted and a person at the robot unmutes. Also carried on daemon_status, which is the copy that survives a daemon outage.

battery_percent.description: Bridge-injected. null means UNKNOWN -- never render it as 0.

servo_temps.description: Per-motor servo CASE temperature in whole degrees C, from the daemon's 1 Hz over-temp sweep (arms + lifts + wheels). A motor ABSENT from the map failed its read that cycle -- unknown, never assume cool. The whole field is omitted on the mock and when the over-temp guard is disabled (NORI_OVERTEMP_C=0). Added to the daemon 2026-08-09; schema'd 2026-08-12.

link_stats.description: Robot-side control-channel receive accounting for the window since the previous telemetry frame (added 2026-08-27; A3 gateway). Separates wire loss from robot-side stalls so a watchdog safe_hold can be attributed. rx_gap_max_ms = largest gap between consecutive inbound control-channel messages in the window. seq_seen/seq_missed appear once the client stamps an integer `seq` on its outbound frames: missed counts holes in the sequence, i.e. frames the wire lost. A large rx_gap with seq_missed 0 means the client sent nothing (operator idle) or the robot itself stalled -- NOT network loss. Named link_stats, not link: status.link (lan/wan) and the inbound `link` frame already use that word.

latch_reason.description: Why motion is blocked, as "<kind>:<detail>": "estop:<trip reason>" (operator command / face button), "overtemp:<motor>" (a joint's servo case temp crossed NORI_OVERTEMP_C), "overcurrent:<motor>" (a joint drew excess current too long — I²t-style trip, latched until reset), or "stall:<motor>" (first obstruction-stalled joint). Precedence estop > overtemp > overcurrent > stall. Absent when none is latched. The bare forms carry no detail and exist for older daemons; "obstruction" is legacy and no longer emitted.

link.description: L2 only. The L3 gateway's safety_status() never sets it, so it cannot be required: requiring it rejected every L3 telemetry frame that carries a status block at all.

motor_faults.description: Per-motor problem state currently asserted: <motor> -> either a decoded hardware fault "<names> (0xNN)" (e.g. "overload,overheat (0x24)", the raw hex authoritative and names best-effort), OR the exact sentinel "no response" meaning that motor did not answer the bus for several reads (dropped / lost power). Only problem motors appear; a motor absent from this map AND answering is healthy — the "no response" sentinel exists so a dropped motor is not indistinguishable from a healthy one.
